name: Trade war & tariffs
value: US proposes 20% Section 301 tariff on China
summary: US proposes Section 301 tariffs on 14 partners on 25 Nov, with 20% on China; not yet in force, no retaliation found
state: On 25 Nov the Trump administration proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China, the EU, India, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, with a 20% rate on Chinese imports (The Hill). The China rate could rise to 40% if the US–China truce, now extended to January, fails to produce a deal (Washington Examiner). Mexico and Norway remain under investigation. The duties are proposed, with no start date or retaliation found, so Watch holds; Alert needs broad tariffs in force with retaliation.
for_you: Importers and exporters trading with China, the EU and Asian manufacturing hubs face uncertainty over US costs while the proposals are finalised. Retaliation, if it follows, tends to hit farm goods, cars and industrial inputs first.
rubric_hit: New major tariffs proposed between large economies (20% on China, 14 partners) = Watch; not in force, no retaliation

sources.title: The Hill — Trump administration targets EU, other countries with new global tariffs
Washington Examiner — Trump administration announces new tariffs on 14 countries

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
